title: Annual Salary to Hourly Rate: A Complete Guide for Australian Workers
description: Convert your annual salary to hourly rate with our guide. Learn the formula, tax brackets, superannuation, and how to compare pay across Australia.
salarySummary: For a standard 38-hour week, your annual salary is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year.

faqs.q: How do I convert my annual salary to an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Divide your annual salary by 52 weeks, then by your weekly hours. For a 38-hour week, hourly rate = annual salary / (38 × 52).

faqs.q: Does the hourly rate include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). Your hourly rate is your base pay before super.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries and occupations by the Fair Work Commission.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Conversion

When you see a job ad with an annual salary or need to compare your hourly rate to a full-time offer, the conversion is straightforward. The formula for **annual salary to hourly rate** is: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For most full-time roles, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman for the standard working week. This gives you a gross annual figure before tax and other deductions.

If you already have an annual salary and want to find your hourly equivalent, divide the salary by 52 weeks, then divide by your weekly hours. For example, a $70,000 annual salary divided by 52 weeks gives $1,346.15 per week. Divide that by 38 hours to get $35.43 per hour. This method works for any weekly hours, but always check your employment contract or award for your actual ordinary hours.

## The Formula Explained

The core formula is: **Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It also assumes you are paid for 52 weeks a year, which is standard for full-time and part-time employees. For casual employees, the same formula applies to your base rate, but you may also receive a 25% casual loading on top.

Your fortnightly pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For a 38-hour week at $30 per hour, your weekly pay is $1,140, so your fortnightly pay is $2,280. This can help you budget if you are paid fortnightly, which is common in Australia.

## Tax and Medicare

Once you have your annual gross pay, you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates from the Australian Taxation Office. The tax-free threshold is $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. You also pay the Medicare levy, generally 2% of your taxable income. Note that the Medicare levy reduction thresholds used here are from 2025–26, as the 2026–27 figures were not confirmed at the time of this guide. For a more detailed estimate of your take-home pay, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

## Superannuation on Top

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means if your hourly rate is $30, your employer pays an extra $3.60 per hour into your super fund. Super is not deducted from your hourly rate; it is an additional cost to the employer. For more details, visit our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

## Casual Loading and Award Rates

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. When using our timesheet, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool calculates it for you. The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. With casual loading, that becomes $33.05 per hour.

Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries and occupations. They often include penalty rates for weekends, nights, and public holidays. The National Minimum Wage applies only to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Always check your award or agreement for your correct minimum rate. For a list of pay guides, see our [pay guides](/blog) page.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Ordinary-time earnings vary across states and territories due to differences in industry mix, cost of living, and local labour markets. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, the national average weekly ordinary-time earnings for full-time adults was $2,083.70 in May 2026. This is an average across all states and industries, not a median for any specific job. For all employees (including part-time), the average weekly total earnings was $1,579.20. State-specific averages are available from the ABS, but they are not reproduced here because they are averages, not job medians. If you need a pay comparison for your occupation, refer to industry-specific award rates or the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page.

When converting your **annual salary to hourly rate**, remember that these averages include a mix of full-time and part-time workers. Your own rate may be higher or lower depending on your role, experience, and location. For a personalised estimate, use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool.

## Important Disclaimer

The annual pay shown here is an estimate based on the formula hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. Always consult a qualified professional for your specific situation.
